1	package cli
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"fmt"
6		"io"
7		"strings"
8	
9		"charm.land/huh/v2"
10	
11		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/agent"
12		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/interactive"
13		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/logging"
14		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/onboarding"
15	)
16	
17	// onboardingSetupMode is the answer to enable's single consent prompt.
18	type onboardingSetupMode int
19	
20	const (
21		// setupModeSkip declines the offers this once — tracking continues either
22		// way; the closing checklist carries the run-later commands and re-running
23		// enable re-offers whatever is still missing. Deliberately the zero value:
24		// a forgotten or defaulted mode must never run login or mirror creation.
25		setupModeSkip onboardingSetupMode = iota
26		// setupModeAll runs every missing rung back-to-back without further questions.
27		setupModeAll
28		// setupModeStepByStep confirms each missing rung individually.
29		setupModeStepByStep
30	)
31	
32	// onboardingOfferRunner drives the connect rungs at the end of `entire
33	// enable`: one consent prompt, then offers for whatever is missing, then the
34	// closing checklist. Rung state is recomputed before each offer, so a login
35	// completed in this pass unblocks the mirror rung in the same pass, and a
36	// rung finished out-of-band is never re-offered — which is also what makes
37	// re-running `entire enable` the resume path after an interrupted setup.
38	// All fields are seams; newOnboardingOfferRunner wires production behavior.
39	type onboardingOfferRunner struct {
40		deps onboardingRungDeps
41		// offerFns runs a rung's setup step; granular=true (step-by-step mode)
42		// lets an offer present its own finer-grained picker.
43		offerFns map[string]func(ctx context.Context, granular bool) error
44		// selfPrompting marks offers that present their own confirmation UI in
45		// granular mode (the import picker), so runOffers skips the generic
46		// yes/no confirm instead of asking twice.
47		selfPrompting map[string]bool
48		// autoRun marks rungs whose offer runs without a prompt when prompting is
49		// unavailable — --yes ("accept all defaults") auto-imports, matching the
50		// enable-time import contract; login/mirror are never implicit.
51		autoRun     map[string]bool
52		canPrompt   func() bool
53		promptMode  func(ctx context.Context, missing []onboarding.Result) (onboardingSetupMode, error)
54		confirmRung func(ctx context.Context, r onboarding.Result) (bool, error)
55		styles      func(w io.Writer) statusStyles
56	}
57	
58	func (r onboardingOfferRunner) run(ctx context.Context, w io.Writer) {
59		ladder := onboardingLadder(r.deps)
60		results := ladder.Checks(ctx)
61	
62		if actionable := r.offerable(results); len(actionable) > 0 && r.canPrompt() {
63			mode, err := r.promptMode(ctx, actionable)
64			if err != nil {
65				// Cancelling the consent prompt (Ctrl-C) behaves like skip: enable
66				// has already succeeded, so fall through to the checklist, whose
67				// hints are the resume path. Logged so a broken terminal doesn't
68				// masquerade as a user choice.
69				logging.Debug(ctx, "onboarding: consent prompt did not complete", "error", err)
70				mode = setupModeSkip
71			}
72			if mode != setupModeSkip {
73				r.runOffers(ctx, w, ladder, mode)
74				results = ladder.Checks(ctx)
75			}
76		} else if r.runAutoOffers(ctx, w, ladder) {
77			results = ladder.Checks(ctx)
78		}
79	
80		fmt.Fprint(w, r.renderChecklist(w, results))
81	}
82	
83	// runAutoOffers runs the autoRun rungs' offers when the prompt path didn't
84	// execute (no TTY or --yes). Reports whether any offer ran.
85	func (r onboardingOfferRunner) runAutoOffers(ctx context.Context, w io.Writer, ladder onboarding.Ladder) bool {
86		ran := false
87		for _, rung := range ladder {
88			offer := r.offerFns[rung.Key]
89			if offer == nil || !r.autoRun[rung.Key] {
90				continue
91			}
92			if rung.Check(ctx).State != onboarding.StateMissing {
93				continue
94			}
95			ran = true
96			if err := offer(ctx, false); err != nil {
97				logging.Warn(ctx, "onboarding: auto offer failed", "rung", rung.Key, "error", err)
98				fmt.Fprintf(w, "  %s setup didn't complete: %v\n", rung.Title, err)
99			}
100		}
101		return ran
102	}
103	
104	// offerable filters the remaining work down to rungs this runner can act on.
105	// Missing rungs with an offer always qualify. Blocked rungs qualify only when
106	// an offerable Missing rung precedes them in the ladder — an earlier offer in
107	// the same pass (login) can unblock them. Without that, the consent prompt
108	// would promise work that can never run (e.g. auth Unknown leaves mirror
109	// Blocked with nothing to unblock it).
110	func (r onboardingOfferRunner) offerable(results []onboarding.Result) []onboarding.Result {
111		var actionable []onboarding.Result
112		unblockPossible := false
113		for _, res := range results {
114			if res.Check.State == onboarding.StateMissing && r.offerFns[res.Rung.Key] != nil {
115				actionable = append(actionable, res)
116				unblockPossible = true
117				continue
118			}
119			if res.Check.State == onboarding.StateBlocked && r.offerFns[res.Rung.Key] != nil && unblockPossible {
120				actionable = append(actionable, res)
121			}
122		}
123		return actionable
124	}
125	
126	// runOffers walks the ladder in order, re-checking each rung immediately
127	// before its offer. Offers are best-effort: a failure prints a notice and
128	// the closing checklist keeps the retry hint, but enable never fails.
129	func (r onboardingOfferRunner) runOffers(ctx context.Context, w io.Writer, ladder onboarding.Ladder, mode onboardingSetupMode) {
130		granular := mode == setupModeStepByStep
131		for _, rung := range ladder {
132			offer := r.offerFns[rung.Key]
133			if offer == nil {
134				continue
135			}
136			check := rung.Check(ctx)
137			if check.State != onboarding.StateMissing {
138				continue
139			}
140			if granular && !r.selfPrompting[rung.Key] {
141				accepted, err := r.confirmRung(ctx, onboarding.Result{Rung: rung, Check: check})
142				if err != nil {
143					// A failed confirm (Ctrl-C, broken terminal, cancelled ctx)
144					// means the user is bailing out — stop walking rungs instead
145					// of surfacing every remaining prompt one Ctrl-C at a time.
146					logging.Debug(ctx, "onboarding: rung confirm prompt did not complete; stopping offers", "rung", rung.Key, "error", err)
147					return
148				}
149				if !accepted {
150					continue
151				}
152			}
153			if err := offer(ctx, granular); err != nil {
154				logging.Warn(ctx, "onboarding: offer failed", "rung", rung.Key, "error", err)
155				fmt.Fprintf(w, "  %s setup didn't complete: %v\n", rung.Title, err)
156			}
157		}
158	}
159	
160	func (r onboardingOfferRunner) renderChecklist(w io.Writer, results []onboarding.Result) string {
161		sty := r.styles(w)
162		var b strings.Builder
163		b.WriteString(renderOnboardingChecklist(results, sty))
164		// One "run later" line per unique command, in ladder order — a blocked
165		// rung whose fix is another rung's command (mirror needs login) must not
166		// repeat it.
167		seen := map[string]bool{}
168		for _, res := range onboarding.Missing(results) {
169			if res.Check.Hint == "" || seen[res.Check.Hint] {
170				continue
171			}
172			seen[res.Check.Hint] = true
173			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "  run later: %s\n", sty.render(sty.cyan, res.Check.Hint))
174		}
175		return b.String()
176	}
177	
178	// enableOnboardingOpts carries the enable-path context the ladder needs.
179	type enableOnboardingOpts struct {
180		// assumeYes: --yes, "accept all defaults" — suppresses prompts.
181		assumeYes bool
182		// neverPrompt: the --agent path's documented non-interactive contract —
183		// suppresses prompts without auto-running anything.
184		neverPrompt bool
185		// firstRun gates --yes auto-import: on the very first enable, --yes
186		// auto-imports (the enable-time import contract); on any later enable it
187		// must not, because "unimported history exists" cannot distinguish "new
188		// history" from "history the user explicitly declined to import".
189		// Interactive re-enables still offer — consent is explicit there.
190		firstRun bool
191		// importScope narrows the import offer to specific agents (the
192		// just-selected ones, or the --agent target). Nil means every agent
193		// with hooks installed — the resume-path scope.
194		importScope []agent.Agent
195	}
196	
197	// newEnableOnboardingRunner applies enableOnboardingOpts to the production
198	// runner. Split from runEnableOnboarding so the option→runner mapping is
199	// unit-testable without network or keyring access.
200	func newEnableOnboardingRunner(w io.Writer, o enableOnboardingOpts) onboardingOfferRunner {
201		r := newOnboardingOfferRunner(w, o.importScope)
202		if o.assumeYes || o.neverPrompt {
203			r.canPrompt = func() bool { return false }
204		}
205		if o.assumeYes && o.firstRun {
206			// Import is local-only, so "accept all defaults" may run it without
207			// a prompt; login and mirror are never implicit.
208			r.autoRun = map[string]bool{onboarding.KeyImport: true}
209		}
210		return r
211	}
212	
213	// runEnableOnboarding runs the connect ladder at the end of `entire enable`.
214	// Best-effort by design: onboarding problems never fail enable.
215	var runEnableOnboarding = func(ctx context.Context, w io.Writer, o enableOnboardingOpts) {
216		// The user explicitly asked for setup — retry probes that recently
217		// failed instead of serving the cached failure (which would silently
218		// suppress the mirror offer for the rest of the failure TTL).
219		defaultMirrorProbeCache().clearUnreachable()
220		r := newEnableOnboardingRunner(w, o)
221		fmt.Fprintln(w)
222		r.run(ctx, w)
223	}
224	
225	// newOnboardingOfferRunner wires the production runner: real rung probes,
226	// the login/mirror/import offers, and huh-based prompts. w is enable's
227	// output writer — offers write their progress there. importScope narrows the
228	// import offer (nil = all agents with hooks installed).
229	func newOnboardingOfferRunner(w io.Writer, importScope []agent.Agent) onboardingOfferRunner {
230		deps := newOnboardingRungDeps()
231		return onboardingOfferRunner{
232			deps: deps,
233			offerFns: map[string]func(ctx context.Context, granular bool) error{
234				onboarding.KeyAuth:   func(ctx context.Context, _ bool) error { return runOnboardingLogin(ctx, w) },
235				onboarding.KeyMirror: func(ctx context.Context, _ bool) error { return runOnboardingMirrorCreate(ctx, w, deps) },
236				onboarding.KeyImport: func(ctx context.Context, granular bool) error {
237					return runOnboardingImport(ctx, w, granular, importScope)
238				},
239			},
240			selfPrompting: map[string]bool{onboarding.KeyImport: true},
241			canPrompt:     interactive.CanPromptInteractively,
242			promptMode:    promptOnboardingSetupMode,
243			confirmRung:   confirmOnboardingRung,
244			styles:        newStatusStyles,
245		}
246	}
247	
248	// promptOnboardingSetupMode is enable's single consent prompt, summarizing
249	// what "finish setup" will do from the missing rungs.
250	func promptOnboardingSetupMode(ctx context.Context, missing []onboarding.Result) (onboardingSetupMode, error) {
251		summary := onboardingSetupSummary(missing)
252		mode := setupModeAll
253		form := NewAccessibleForm(
254			huh.NewGroup(
255				huh.NewSelect[onboardingSetupMode]().
256					Title("Finish setup?").
257					Description(summary).
258					Options(
259						huh.NewOption("Yes, set up everything (recommended)", setupModeAll),
260						huh.NewOption("Choose step by step", setupModeStepByStep),
261						huh.NewOption("Skip for now — finish anytime with `entire enable`", setupModeSkip),
262					).
263					Value(&mode),
264			),
265		)
266		if err := form.RunWithContext(ctx); err != nil {
267			return setupModeSkip, fmt.Errorf("setup consent prompt: %w", err)
268		}
269		return mode, nil
270	}
271	
272	// onboardingSetupSummary describes what the fast path will do, e.g.
273	// "Logs in to entire.io and mirrors this repo so your work shows up in the
274	// web UI."
275	func onboardingSetupSummary(missing []onboarding.Result) string {
276		steps := make([]string, 0, len(missing))
277		for _, r := range missing {
278			switch r.Rung.Key {
279			case onboarding.KeyAuth:
280				steps = append(steps, "logs in to entire.io")
281			case onboarding.KeyMirror:
282				steps = append(steps, "mirrors this repo")
283			case onboarding.KeyImport:
284				steps = append(steps, "imports existing agent history")
285			}
286		}
287		if len(steps) == 0 {
288			return ""
289		}
290		summary := formatTokenClassList(steps)
291		// Capitalize the first step: summaries are full sentences in the prompt.
292		return strings.ToUpper(summary[:1]) + summary[1:] + " so your work shows up in the web UI."
293	}
294	
295	func confirmOnboardingRung(ctx context.Context, r onboarding.Result) (bool, error) {
296		title := r.Rung.Title
297		if r.Check.Detail != "" {
298			title += " — " + r.Check.Detail
299		}
300		confirmed := true
301		form := NewAccessibleForm(
302			huh.NewGroup(
303				huh.NewConfirm().
304					Title(title).
305					Value(&confirmed),
306			),
307		)
308		if err := form.RunWithContext(ctx); err != nil {
309			return false, fmt.Errorf("rung confirm prompt: %w", err)
310		}
311		return confirmed, nil
312	}

1	// Package agentimport imports a coding agent's pre-existing local transcripts
2	// into Entire as read-only, commit-less checkpoints on the v1 metadata branch.
3	//
4	// The orchestration (discovery loop, idempotent per-turn IDs, redaction, and
5	// the checkpoint write) is agent-agnostic and lives here. Each agent plugs in
6	// an Importer that knows where its transcripts live and how to split one into
7	// per-user-prompt turns. Claude Code is the only implementation today
8	// (see claude.go); others register themselves the same way.
9	package agentimport
10	
11	import (
12		"context"
13		"crypto/sha256"
14		"encoding/hex"
15		"fmt"
16		"os"
17		"sort"
18		"time"
19	
20		"github.com/go-git/go-git/v6"
21	
22		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/agent/types"
23		cp "github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint"
24		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/id"
25		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/logging"
26		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/session"
27		"github.com/entireio/cli/redact"
28	)
29	
30	// LookbackDays bounds how far back import reaches. Fixed this pass (no flag).
31	const LookbackDays = 30
32	
33	// SessionFile is one discovered agent transcript for a repo.
34	type SessionFile struct {
35		Path      string // absolute path to the transcript file
36		SessionID string // agent session id (used in checkpoint metadata)
37	}
38	
39	// Turn is one user-prompt turn extracted from a session transcript. Line
40	// offsets are in raw-line space (newline-counted), matching transcript slicing
41	// and the agent token-usage helpers.
42	type Turn struct {
43		LineStart, LineEnd int
44		UUID               string
45		Prompt, Model      string
46		CreatedAt          time.Time
47		Tokens             *types.TokenUsage
48	}
49	
50	// Importer is the per-agent seam: it locates an agent's transcripts for a repo
51	// and splits one into per-turn units. Everything else (idempotency, redaction,
52	// writing) is handled generically by Run.
53	type Importer interface {
54		// Name is the registry key and the provenance source (e.g. "claude-code").
55		Name() string
56		// AgentType is the display name stored in checkpoint metadata (e.g. "Claude Code").
57		AgentType() types.AgentType
58		// Discover returns the agent's transcript files for the repo within the
59		// lookback window. overridePath replaces the default transcript dir;
60		// sessionFilter, when non-empty, keeps only matching session IDs.
61		Discover(repoRoot, overridePath string, now time.Time, sessionFilter []string) ([]SessionFile, error)
62		// SplitTurns splits one session's raw transcript bytes into per-turn units.
63		SplitTurns(sf SessionFile, full []byte) ([]Turn, error)
64	}
65	
66	// importers is the static set of supported agents. Adding an agent is a new
67	// Importer implementation appended here — no init() / runtime registration.
68	var importers = []Importer{
69		claudeImporter{},
70		cursorImporter{},
71		piImporter{},
72		factoryImporter{},
73		codexImporter{},
74		copilotImporter{},
75		geminiImporter{},
76	}
77	
78	// All returns every supported importer, sorted by name.
79	func All() []Importer {
80		out := append([]Importer(nil), importers...)
81		sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool { return out[i].Name() < out[j].Name() })
82		return out
83	}
84	
85	// Options configures an import run.
86	type Options struct {
87		RepoRoot      string
88		OverridePath  string
89		SessionFilter []string
90		Now           time.Time
91		DryRun        bool
92	}
93	
94	// Result summarizes an import run.
95	type Result struct {
96		SessionsScanned int
97		TurnsImported   int
98		TurnsSkipped    int
99	}
100	
101	// DeriveCheckpointID produces a stable 12-hex checkpoint ID for an imported
102	// turn. Re-importing the same (sessionID, turnUUID) yields the same ID, which
103	// is how import stays idempotent.
104	func DeriveCheckpointID(sessionID, turnUUID string) id.CheckpointID {
105		sum := sha256.Sum256([]byte(sessionID + "/" + turnUUID))
106		return id.MustCheckpointID(hex.EncodeToString(sum[:6])) // 6 bytes = 12 lowercase hex chars
107	}
108	
109	// Run imports the given agent's transcripts (within the lookback window) as
110	// read-only checkpoints on the v1 metadata branch (Kind "imported"). It is
111	// idempotent: turns whose deterministic ID already exists are skipped.
112	func Run(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, imp Importer, opts Options) (Result, error) {
113		var res Result
114		files, err := imp.Discover(opts.RepoRoot, opts.OverridePath, opts.Now, opts.SessionFilter)
115		if err != nil {
116			return res, fmt.Errorf("discover %s sessions: %w", imp.Name(), err)
117		}
118	
119		stores, err := cp.Open(ctx, repo, cp.OpenOptions{})
120		if err != nil {
121			return res, fmt.Errorf("open checkpoint store: %w", err)
122		}
123		existing := make(map[string]bool)
124		if infos, listErr := stores.Persistent.List(ctx); listErr == nil {
125			for _, in := range infos {
126				existing[in.CheckpointID.String()] = true
127			}
128		}
129	
130		for _, sf := range files {
131			res.SessionsScanned++
132			full, readErr := os.ReadFile(sf.Path)
133			if readErr != nil {
134				return res, fmt.Errorf("read %s: %w", sf.Path, readErr)
135			}
136			turns, splitErr := imp.SplitTurns(sf, full)
137			if splitErr != nil {
138				return res, fmt.Errorf("split %s session %s: %w", imp.Name(), sf.SessionID, splitErr)
139			}
140			// Redact the session transcript once and reuse it for every turn's
141			// checkpoint (each turn stores the full session transcript with its own
142			// CheckpointTranscriptStart). Redacting per turn would be O(turns).
143			// Computed lazily so a fully-skipped or dry-run file pays nothing.
144			var red redact.RedactedBytes
145			redacted := false
146			for _, turn := range turns {
147				cid := DeriveCheckpointID(sf.SessionID, turn.UUID)
148				if existing[cid.String()] {
149					res.TurnsSkipped++
150					continue
151				}
152				if opts.DryRun {
153					res.TurnsImported++ // counts what would import
154					continue
155				}
156				if !redacted {
157					r, rerr := redact.JSONLBytes(full)
158					if rerr != nil {
159						return res, fmt.Errorf("redact %s transcript: %w", sf.SessionID, rerr)
160					}
161					red = r
162					redacted = true
163				}
164				if err := writeTurn(ctx, stores, imp, cid, sf, red, turn); err != nil {
165					return res, err
166				}
167				existing[cid.String()] = true
168				res.TurnsImported++
169			}
170	
171			// Track A: surface this session in `entire session list`. Best-effort —
172			// the read-only checkpoints above are the primary artifact, so a
173			// state-write failure must not abort the import.
174			if !opts.DryRun {
175				if serr := writeSessionState(ctx, imp, sf, turns); serr != nil {
176					logging.Debug(ctx, "import: failed to write imported session state",
177						"sessionID", sf.SessionID, "error", serr.Error())
178				}
179			}
180		}
181		return res, nil
182	}
183	
184	// writeSessionState upserts a local session.State so an imported session shows
185	// up in `entire session list`. It is Kind-gated (KindImported), never sets
186	// BaseCommit (imports are commit-less and must not be pinned to HEAD), and uses
187	// the transcript's own timestamps — the forward-compat contract that keeps a
188	// later commit-SHA link purely additive. It never clobbers a live or
189	// manually-attached session that happens to share the ID.
190	func writeSessionState(ctx context.Context, imp Importer, sf SessionFile, turns []Turn) error {
191		if len(turns) == 0 {
192			return nil
193		}
194		store, err := session.NewStateStore(ctx)
195		if err != nil {
196			return fmt.Errorf("open session state store: %w", err)
197		}
198		if existing, lerr := store.Load(ctx, sf.SessionID); lerr == nil && existing != nil &&
199			!existing.Kind.IsImported() {
200			return nil // don't overwrite a real (live/attached) session
201		}
202	
203		var started, ended time.Time
204		var tokens *types.TokenUsage
205		model := ""
206		for _, turn := range turns {
207			if !turn.CreatedAt.IsZero() {
208				if started.IsZero() || turn.CreatedAt.Before(started) {
209					started = turn.CreatedAt
210				}
211				if turn.CreatedAt.After(ended) {
212					ended = turn.CreatedAt
213				}
214			}
215			if turn.Model != "" {
216				model = turn.Model
217			}
218			tokens = types.AddTokenUsage(tokens, turn.Tokens)
219		}
220		if started.IsZero() {
221			// No usable per-turn timestamps (some Codex lines): fall back to the
222			// transcript file mtime so the row still sorts sensibly. Never "now".
223			if fi, statErr := os.Stat(sf.Path); statErr == nil {
224				started = fi.ModTime()
225				ended = started
226			}
227		}
228		state := &session.State{
229			SessionID:           sf.SessionID,
230			Kind:                session.KindImported,
231			AgentType:           imp.AgentType(),
232			ModelName:           model,
233			StartedAt:           started,
234			EndedAt:             &ended,
235			Phase:               session.PhaseEnded,
236			LastInteractionTime: &ended,
237			StepCount:           len(turns),
238			TokenUsage:          tokens,
239			LastPrompt:          session.TruncatePromptForStorage(turns[len(turns)-1].Prompt),
240			LastCheckpointID:    DeriveCheckpointID(sf.SessionID, turns[len(turns)-1].UUID),
241		}
242		if err := store.Save(ctx, state); err != nil {
243			return fmt.Errorf("save imported session state %s: %w", sf.SessionID, err)
244		}
245		return nil
246	}
247	
248	func writeTurn(ctx context.Context, stores *cp.Stores, imp Importer, cid id.CheckpointID, sf SessionFile, red redact.RedactedBytes, turn Turn) error {
249		if err := stores.Persistent.Write(ctx, cp.Session(cp.WriteOptions{
250			CheckpointID:              cid,
251			SessionID:                 sf.SessionID,
252			CreatedAt:                 turn.CreatedAt,
253			Strategy:                  "import",
254			Kind:                      string(session.KindImported),
255			Agent:                     imp.AgentType(),
256			Model:                     turn.Model,
257			Transcript:                red,
258			Prompts:                   []string{turn.Prompt},
259			CheckpointsCount:          1,
260			CheckpointTranscriptStart: turn.LineStart,
261			TokenUsage:                turn.Tokens,
262		})); err != nil {
263			return fmt.Errorf("write imported checkpoint %s: %w", cid, err)
264		}
265		return nil
266	}

explain first

Pausing there — I'd made one small edit (added imports to `onboarding_rungs.go`); nothing functional has changed yet. Here's the full picture.

## Bug 1: "Imported 2 turn(s)" followed by "✗ History … not imported"

The flow itself is correct — `entire enable` re-runs the ladder checks *after* the offers complete (`onboarding_offer.go:74`). The stale ✗ comes from the import rung's **scan cache** (`~/.cache/entire/onboarding_imports.json`).

The rung's dry-run scan is expensive (opens the checkpoint store, parses every transcript), so `discoverAgentImports` memoizes it behind a fingerprint of:

1. the discovered transcript files' path/mtime/size, and
2. `metadataBranchTip(repo)` — the tip of the **`entire/checkpoints/v1` branch**, on the theory that "any new checkpoint or import moves the ref" (`onboarding_rungs.go:287`, `onboarding_import_cache.go:14-20`).

That theory broke when the **git-refs checkpoint backend** landed. This repo's `.entire/settings.json` has:

```json
"checkpoints": { "primary": { "type": "git-refs" } }
```

Under a git-refs primary, imported checkpoints are written as per-checkpoint refs at `refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/<id>` — **the v1 branch never moves**. So within one `enable` run:

1. Pre-offer check scans, caches "2 sessions, 2 unimported turns" under fingerprint F.
2. Import offer runs, writes 2 checkpoints to refs. Transcript files unchanged, branch tip unchanged → fingerprint still F.
3. Post-offer re-check hits the cache → serves the stale "not imported" statuses → "✗ History".

On a cache *miss* the fresh dry-run would be correct — its dedup (`agentimport.Run`) lists checkpoints through the kind-routing store, which unions both backends. Only the fingerprint is blind to refs. This also means a manual `entire import claude-code` followed by `entire status` shows the same stale ✗ until a transcript file changes.

**Proposed fix:** add a second component to the fingerprint — an order-independent digest of all local refs under `refs/entire/checkpoints/` (name + hash). If ref iteration fails, mark the scan uncacheable rather than risking a false hit. Plus a regression test.

## Bug 2: "Imports existing agent history so your work shows up in the web UI."

That sentence comes from `onboardingSetupSummary` (`onboarding_offer.go:275-293`), which builds the consent-prompt description by listing the missing steps and appending one blanket benefit clause — `"… so your work shows up in the web UI."` — regardless of which steps are in the list. When import is the only missing rung, the whole claim rides on import, and it's false: imported checkpoints are local (they do get *enqueued* for the pre-push batch under git-refs, but the web UI doesn't render imported sessions at all today). The `entire import` command's own help is already honest: "searchable and explainable but not rewindable."

**Proposed fix:** split the summary — login/mirror keep "so your work shows up in the web UI"; the import step gets its own honest clause, something like "imports existing agent history so past sessions show up in `entire session list`". Two sentences when both groups are present.

## The recent imported-sessions work you mentioned

- The session-list surfacing (PR #1699, `writeSessionState` in `agentimport`) is already merged into this branch — that's the local `entire session list` visibility, which is what the corrected copy should point at.
- This branch is missing two `agentimport` fixes that are on `origin/main`: `440c0adaf` (stop summing cumulative subagent tokens across imported turns) and `1e53147e9` (keep subagent baseline when a turn's snapshot is nil). Both are token-accounting fixes, not web-UI visibility — they'd come in with the next merge of main into `cli-onboard`.
- Nothing on main makes imported sessions web-visible, so the copy fix stands regardless.

One open question on the copy: do you want the import clause to say `entire session list` specifically, different wording, or just drop the benefit clause for import entirely? And should I also merge `origin/main` into this branch while I'm at it, or leave that separate?
yes merge main branch, and just keep everything from 1699 as is, don't change anything from that we're extending onboarding with just login, mirroring basicaly

yes merge main branch, and just keep everything from 1699 as is, don't change anything from that we're extending onboarding with just login, mirroring basicaly - adn then the status if you're not done onboarding

Got it — scope stays as-is: onboarding = login + mirror (plus the status checklist when setup is incomplete), the #1699 imported-sessions behavior untouched. I'll merge `origin/main` in first, then fix the stale History mark (fingerprint) and the summary copy so the web-UI claim only attaches to login/mirror.

input.content:
---
name: go-test-json-stderr-swap
description: Go 1.26 `go test -json` (gotestsum, mise run test) replaces the os.Stderr variable after package init — pointer comparisons against os.Stderr fail only in json mode
metadata:
  type: reference
---

Under Go 1.26, `go test -json` (which gotestsum — and therefore `mise run test` — uses) replaces the `os.Stderr` *variable* after package init with an attribution pipe (its `Fd()` reports 1). A package-level `var w = os.Stderr` captured at init keeps the real fd-2 file, so `w == os.Stderr` is true under plain `go test` but false under `-json`. Symptom: a test fails only via `mise run test` / gotestsum while passing when run directly.

Fix pattern (used in `internal/entireclient/tokenstore/file_test.go` TestLoosePermsWarnWriter_DefaultsToStderr): assert the writer is an `*os.File` whose `Fd() == uintptr(syscall.Stderr)` instead of pointer equality. `syscall.Stderr` is defined on all platforms including Windows.

Related: [[stale-tmux-breaks-e2e]] — the other "fails locally under the harness, not the code" trap.

Done — main is merged in and both onboarding bugs are fixed, committed on `cli-onboard` (not pushed).

## What was wrong

**The stale "✗ History" mark.** The enable flow *does* re-check the ladder after the import runs — the problem was the import rung's memoized scan cache. Its invalidation fingerprint only watched the `entire/checkpoints/v1` **branch tip**, but this repo's `.entire/settings.json` configures the **git-refs** checkpoint primary, where imports write `refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/<id>` and never move that branch. Unchanged fingerprint → the re-check served the pre-import "2 sessions found, not imported" cache entry right after printing "Imported 2 turn(s)". The same staleness hit `entire status` after a manual `entire import claude-code`. Fixed by folding an order-independent digest of the per-checkpoint refs into the fingerprint (`826c6ce38`), with a regression test that creates a checkpoint ref and asserts the tip moves.

**The false web-UI promise.** `onboardingSetupSummary` appended "so your work shows up in the web UI." to whatever steps were missing, including import. Now login/mirror keep the web-UI clause and import gets its own honest one — "imports existing agent history so past sessions show up in entire session list" — matching what #1699 actually delivers (`c0c040951`). Nothing from #1699 itself was touched.

**Bonus fix found during verification.** `mise run test` was failing on main-merged code in `tokenstore`: Go 1.26's `go test -json` (what gotestsum runs) swaps the `os.Stderr` variable after package init, breaking a pointer-equality assertion that passes under plain `go test`. Pinned the test by file descriptor instead (`8146a3137`).

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The checkpoint layer's two coexisting backends mean "the metadata ref moved" is no longer one fact — any cache keyed on the v1 branch tip alone silently goes stale for git-refs writes. Worth auditing if other caches adopt that pattern.
- The Go 1.26 stderr swap only manifests under `-json`, so "passes with `go test`, fails with `mise run test`" is now a signature to recognize, not a flake.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

The merge from `origin/main` also brought in the two imported-session token-accounting fixes this branch was missing (`440c0adaf`, `1e53147e9`); the merge conflict in `setup.go` was resolved to keep both main's `useProject` scope fix and this branch's onboarding hook. Full `mise run check` (unit + integration + e2e canary) passes. I left the branch unpushed — say the word if you want it pushed to update the PR/trail.

# E2E validation of the onboarding History rung under a git-refs checkpoint
# primary, in a fully isolated fresh repo. Repro of the trail-742 report:
# enable caches "not imported", import writes checkpoint refs (branch tip
# unmoved), re-check must NOT serve the stale cache entry.
set -euo pipefail

SB="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
BIN="$SB/entire"
REPO="$SB/repo"
rm -rf "$SB/repo" "$SB/home" "$SB/config" "$SB/cache" "$SB/claude-projects" "$SB/tokens.json"
mkdir -p "$REPO" "$SB/home" "$SB/config" "$SB/cache" "$SB/claude-projects"

run() { # run entire fully isolated + non-interactive
  (cd "$REPO" && env \
    HOME="$SB/home" \
    ENTIRE_CONFIG_DIR="$SB/config" \
    XDG_CACHE_HOME="$SB/cache" \
    ENTIRE_TOKEN_STORE=file \
    ENTIRE_TOKEN_STORE_PATH="$SB/tokens.json" \
    ENTIRE_TEST_AUTH_STORE_FILE="$SB/auth-store.json" \
    ENTIRE_TEST_CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR="$SB/claude-projects" \
    GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 \
    "$BIN" "$@")
}

echo "=== 1. fresh repo (git-refs checkpoint primary, fake GitHub origin)"
git -C "$REPO" init -q -b main
git -C "$REPO" config user.name "Test User"
git -C "$REPO" config user.email "test@example.com"
git -C "$REPO" config commit.gpgsign false
echo "# fresh" > "$REPO/README.md"
git -C "$REPO" add README.md
git -C "$REPO" commit -qm "init"
git -C "$REPO" remote add origin git@github.com:acme/fresh-onboard-test.git
mkdir -p "$REPO/.entire"
cat > "$REPO/.entire/settings.json" << 'JSON'
{
  "checkpoints": { "primary": { "type": "git-refs" } }
}
JSON

echo "=== 2. seed two fake Claude Code sessions (recent, discoverable)"
TS_DATE="$(date -u -v-2d +%Y-%m-%d 2>/dev/null || date -u -d '2 days ago' +%Y-%m-%d)"
for S in s-alpha s-beta; do
  cat > "$SB/claude-projects/$S.jsonl" << JSONL
{"type":"user","uuid":"$S-u1","sessionId":"$S","timestamp":"${TS_DATE}T10:00:00Z","cwd":"$REPO","message":{"role":"user","content":"add a hello function ($S)"}}
{"type":"assistant","uuid":"$S-a1","parentUuid":"$S-u1","timestamp":"${TS_DATE}T10:00:05Z","message":{"role":"assistant","model":"claude-sonnet-5","content":[{"type":"text","text":"done"}],"usage":{"input_tokens":12,"output_tokens":7}}}
JSONL
done
ls -la "$SB/claude-projects/"

echo
echo "=== 3. entire enable --agent claude-code --yes (expect: History ✗ '2 ... found, not imported' — populates scan cache)"
run enable --agent claude-code --yes 2>&1 | tee "$SB/out-enable-1.txt"

echo
echo "=== 4. v1 branch tip + checkpoint refs BEFORE import"
git -C "$REPO" rev-parse --verify -q refs/heads/entire/checkpoints/v1 > "$SB/v1-before.txt" || echo "none" > "$SB/v1-before.txt"
cat "$SB/v1-before.txt"
git -C "$REPO" for-each-ref 'refs/entire/checkpoints/**' | tee "$SB/refs-before.txt" || true

echo
echo "=== 5. entire import claude-code (expect: 2 turns imported)"
run import claude-code 2>&1 | tee "$SB/out-import.txt"

echo
echo "=== 6. v1 branch tip + checkpoint refs AFTER import (tip must be unchanged; refs must exist)"
git -C "$REPO" rev-parse --verify -q refs/heads/entire/checkpoints/v1 > "$SB/v1-after.txt" || echo "none" > "$SB/v1-after.txt"
cat "$SB/v1-after.txt"
git -C "$REPO" for-each-ref 'refs/entire/checkpoints/**' | tee "$SB/refs-after.txt"

echo
echo "=== 7. entire status (THE BUG CHECK: History must be ✓ '2 sessions imported', not stale ✗)"
run status 2>&1 | tee "$SB/out-status.txt"

echo
echo "=== 8. entire enable resume path (checklist must also show History done)"
run enable --agent claude-code --yes 2>&1 | tee "$SB/out-enable-2.txt"

echo
echo "=== VERDICT"
fail=0
grep -q "claude-code sessions found, not imported" "$SB/out-enable-1.txt" \
  && echo "PASS: pre-import checklist reported unimported history (cache populated)" \
  || { echo "FAIL: pre-import checklist missing 'not imported' row"; fail=1; }
grep -Eq "Imported 2 turn" "$SB/out-import.txt" \
  && echo "PASS: import wrote 2 turns" || { echo "FAIL: import did not report 2 turns"; fail=1; }
if [ "$(cat "$SB/v1-before.txt")" = "$(cat "$SB/v1-after.txt")" ]; then
  echo "PASS: v1 branch tip unchanged by import (git-refs primary confirmed)"
else
  echo "NOTE: v1 branch tip moved — scenario not git-refs-shaped"
fi
[ -s "$SB/refs-after.txt" ] && echo "PASS: per-checkpoint refs written under refs/entire/checkpoints/" \
  || { echo "FAIL: no checkpoint refs found"; fail=1; }
grep -q "sessions imported" "$SB/out-status.txt" \
  && echo "PASS: status shows History done ('sessions imported')" \
  || { echo "FAIL: status does not show imported History"; fail=1; }
grep -q "not imported" "$SB/out-status.txt" \
  && { echo "FAIL: status still shows stale 'not imported' (THE BUG)"; fail=1; } \
  || echo "PASS: no stale 'not imported' row after import"
exit $fail

Ran a live end-to-end test in a fully isolated fresh repository (own `HOME`, `ENTIRE_CONFIG_DIR`, `XDG_CACHE_HOME`, file token store, fake `github.com` origin, `git-refs` checkpoint primary, two seeded Claude Code transcripts) — and an A/B against the pre-fix binary.

| `entire enable --agent claude-code --yes` shows `✗ History — 2 claude-code sessions found, not imported` (cache populated) | PASS |

| `entire status` shows `✓ History — 2 sessions imported` | PASS |

**Pre-fix binary (merge commit `415ea4489`), same scenario:** identical setup and import succeed, but `entire status` afterwards still shows the stale `✗ History — 2 claude-code sessions found, not imported` — the exact bug from the trail report, reproduced and confirmed fixed by the fingerprint change.

**Overall: PASS**

so is the x history, not imported fix done?

Yes, done end to end:

- **Fixed** in `826c6ce38` — the import-scan cache fingerprint now includes the git-refs per-checkpoint refs, so an import invalidates it even though the v1 branch tip doesn't move. The related copy fix ("so your work shows up in the web UI" no longer attached to import) is `c0c040951`.
- **Pushed** — both are on `origin/cli-onboard`, so the trail/PR has them.
- **Verified three ways:** unit regression tests (`TestMetadataTip_MovesWithCheckpointRefs`, summary copy cases), the full `mise run check` suite (unit + integration + e2e canary), and the live fresh-repo A/B you just saw — the pre-fix binary reproduces the stale `✗ History` after a successful import; the fixed binary shows `✓ History — 2 sessions imported` in both `entire status` and the `entire enable` resume checklist.

One caveat on your original repro: the fix changes cache *invalidation*, so it heals existing stale entries on its own — the repo where you saw the bug will show `✓ History` on the next `entire status` with the new binary, no cache cleanup needed.

All three trail findings are addressed and resolved — the trail now shows zero open findings.

**Finding 1 (medium, 0.75) — suspended empty-upstream mirror cached as green.** Real bug. `createAndAwaitMirror` wrote the probe cache right after `CreateMirror` based on its `Suspended` flag, but for an existing empty-upstream placement suspension only surfaces via the follow-up `GetMirror` read — so the checklist could show "✓ Repo mirrored" for the 15-minute TTL on a mirror that never serves. Fixed in `b7a33f3ba`: the write-through (now `healMirrorProbeCache`) runs only after every suspension signal is checked, with an httptest-backed regression test covering both the suspended (error, no cache write) and serving (cache healed) empty-upstream cases.

**Finding 2 (low, 0.55) — multi-agent import hint names only the first agent.** Real. Fixed in `fcdbe7744`: one pending agent keeps the direct `entire import claude-code` hint; several pending agents now get `entire import`, whose help lists the per-agent subcommands, so following the hint can't look like the whole step is done. Unit test added.

**Finding 3 (medium, 0.55) — `ListAvailableMirrors` can't express suspension, so the rung flips green.** Already fixed before this session by `596661d3d` (the review system had marked it stale): `probeMirrorAcross` follows up a "mirrored" answer with `mirrorSuspendedOn`, the suspended flag is cached, and the rung renders "Blocked — mirror suspended by an admin". Resolved with that reference, no code change needed.

They're the "did the import actually land, and where" pair — one user-facing view, one raw-storage view:

**`entire-demo checkpoint list`** — the user-facing catalog. In your demo you'll see two entries marked `[imported]`, one per imported turn, each showing its checkpoint ID and the original prompt from your seeded sessions ("add a hello endpoint to the server" / "write unit tests for the hello endpoint") with the transcript's own timestamp — proof the old sessions became real, browsable checkpoints you can `entire-demo explain`.

**`git for-each-ref refs/entire/checkpoints`** — the raw storage, and it's there to show what the wizard's storage choice actually did. Because you'll pick **refs** in the checkpoint-storage step, each checkpoint is stored as its own git ref (`refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/<id>` pointing at a metadata commit) instead of as commits stacked on the `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch. You'll see two lines, whose IDs match the two from `checkpoint list`.

That second one is also the punchline of the bug you reported: under this backend an import moves *these refs* and never the v1 branch tip — which is exactly why the old binary's History rung kept serving its stale "not imported" answer, and why the fixed one notices immediately. (If you'd picked "branch" in the wizard instead, `for-each-ref` would print nothing and the import would show up as commits on `entire/checkpoints/v1`.)

Fixed, tested, pushed (`a8272eb1d`), and the demo is reset to a blank slate for a clean re-run. To your three points:

**1. Mirror needs the repo to exist first — yes, exactly.** The bootstrap intentionally publishes to GitHub *last* (so the initial commit captures `.entire/` and hook files), but the connect ladder was running before that — at a moment when `origin` doesn't exist yet, so the mirror check could only say "couldn't check" and the offer could never fire. The ladder is now deferred until after publish.

**2. Sequential steps.** The first-run flow now reads as four distinct sections, in order:

```
Setting up git repository   (init, identity, your GitHub choices)
Enabling Entire             (agents, checkpoint storage, hooks, telemetry)
Publishing to GitHub        (initial commit, repo create, push)
Connecting to entire.io     (login → mirror → import, then the checklist)

Done.
```

The consent prompt and each offer still pace themselves (they wait for you), and "step by step" mode confirms each rung individually if the fast path feels too quick.

**3. Mirroring itself: untouched.** `entire repo mirror create/list/get/remove` and the shared `createAndAwaitMirror` machinery are exactly as before — the only thing that moved is *when* enable invokes the same offer. Users who skip it during enable can still mirror later via the command or by re-running `entire enable`, unchanged.

One bonus from your local-only observation: a repo with **no origin remote at all** now shows `– Repo mirrored  no origin remote` instead of the dead-end "couldn't check — retry with `entire repo mirror list`".

1. **Setting up git repository** — git init, your choices gathered (repo name, owner, visibility, push).
2. **Enabling Entire** — agent picker, checkpoint storage picker, hooks, telemetry.
3. **Publishing to GitHub** — initial commit, `gh repo create`, push. *This is the moment `origin` and the GitHub repo come into existence.*
4. **Connecting to entire.io** — the ladder runs only now, so the mirror rung probes a repo that actually exists: login first, then the mirror offer fires ("Mirroring `<owner>/<repo>` to aws-us-east-2.entire.io…"), then the history import, then the closing checklist — which should show all four rungs ✓ in one pass.

Previously step 4 ran before step 3, which is why your first run showed `? Repo mirrored — couldn't check` and mirroring only worked on the second `entire enable`.

The branch-off cases behave sensibly too:

- **You decline the GitHub repo** (local-only): the mirror rung shows `no origin remote` (n/a) instead of the misleading "couldn't check" — and if you later add a GitHub origin, re-running `entire enable` offers mirroring then.
- **Existing repo with an origin** (your original trail scenario): unchanged — the ladder always could probe there; it now just does the same thing in the bootstrap flow.
- **`--yes` / `--agent` non-interactive variants**: same deferred ordering, pinned by a regression test that asserts the ladder sees "Created initial commit" already in the output before it runs.

Fully set up collapses the checklist to one line: `Connected: peyton-alt · mirrored to github.com/peyton-alt/demo-onboarding`. (If you skipped anything, you get the rung-by-rung checklist with the next command instead — that's the "status shows your remaining setup" behavior.)

Expect `Imported 0 turn(s) from 2 session(s) (2 already imported).`

```fish
entire-demo enable
```

Prints "Entire is already enabled" plus the collapsed `Connected: …` line — no prompts, because every rung is done. (This is the same command an interrupted user runs to pick up where they left off.)

Yes — the review had posted one new finding, and it's now handled end to end:

**The finding (medium):** the mirror-probe cache keyed entries by `owner/repo` only, but the probe asks the *active context's* core — so after `entire auth use` the mirror rung could serve the previous identity's cached answer for up to 15 minutes. Legitimate bug.

**The fix (`c698a05db`, pushed):** cache keys now carry an identity scope — the active context name, or a digest of `ENTIRE_TOKEN` for env-token sessions — so a context switch simply misses the cache and re-probes. Covered by `TestMirrorProbeKey_ScopedByAuthIdentity`, full unit suite green, finding resolved on the trail with the commit reference. **Trail 742 is back to zero open findings** (9 resolved total).

It was a flake — CI is fully green now.

What happened: the failure was `TestPartialStaging/vogon` in the git-branch canary on `51cbc4bef` (the merge of main that landed on the branch). The test waits up to 30 seconds for the second commit's condensed checkpoint to appear on the v1 branch, and a busy shared runner blew past that window. Evidence it wasn't real:

- Didn't reproduce locally on the exact same commit — both the isolated test and the full 59-test canary under git-branch pass.
- Main's CI is green with the same merged code, and the git-refs variant of the same job passed even on the failing attempt.
- A plain rerun of the failed jobs just passed: `test-canary (git-branch)` ✓, `test-canary (git-refs)` ✓, aggregate `test` ✓ — the whole Tests run for the branch now concludes `success`.

Nothing to fix in the branch code. If this particular 30-second `WaitForCheckpointExists` bites again on CI, it'd be worth bumping that timeout or investigating condensation latency on slow runners — but one occurrence with a clean rerun doesn't justify touching it now.

Yes — switching after enable is fully supported today, in both directions, and backward compatibility is automatic. Three layers:

**1. The switch is one command:**
```fish
entire configure --checkpoint-backend refs    # or: branch
```
(also `entire enable --checkpoint-backend …` on an already-set-up repo). It just rewrites `checkpoints.primary.type` in `.entire/settings.json`.

**2. Old checkpoints stay readable with zero migration** — this is designed in. The checkpoint store is a routing layer that reads *both* formats side by side: legacy hex-ID checkpoints resolve from the `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch, ULID checkpoints from `refs/entire/checkpoints/…`, and `checkpoint list` unions the two. After a switch, new checkpoints use the new backend while everything prior keeps working (list/explain/rewind). The code's own contract comment: *"Switching the primary on an existing repo is safe: new checkpoints use the new backend while read routing keeps prior checkpoints readable in their original format."*

**3. Optional full migration exists too**: `entire doctor migrate-checkpoints` converts v1-branch checkpoints into per-checkpoint refs — idempotent, safe to re-run, queues the new refs for push. For anyone who wants one clean layout instead of coexistence.

So the answer to "backward compatible or flag?" is **both, already shipped**: trail 1 only removes the *question at setup time* — it doesn't remove choice. New users get refs silently; existing repos keep whatever they have; anyone can flip later with one command and lose nothing; and the deliberate ones can migrate history outright.

That makes trail 1's risk profile small: it's purely a defaults/UX change sitting on top of an existing, tested coexistence mechanism (the same `kindRoutingStore` that CI's canary exercises under both backends). so what does --yes do?

`--yes` on `entire enable` means "accept every default, ask nothing" — but with a deliberate line between local and outward actions:

**What it auto-accepts (local, reversible):**
- **Agents**: selects *all* available agents instead of showing the picker
- **Telemetry**: consents (unless `--telemetry=false` or `ENTIRE_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT`)
- **Checkpoint storage**: the default — with trail 1, that's refs written into settings
- **Bootstrap** (non-git folder): accepts git init, default commit message, creates a *private* GitHub repo under your account, and pushes — explicit flags like `--no-github` still override
- **Import**: on the very first enable only, auto-imports local sessions without the prompt (it's local-only, so consent-by-`--yes` is considered enough; on later re-runs it never auto-imports, because "unimported history" might mean "history you declined")

**What it never does, even with `--yes`:**
- **Log in** — no browser gets opened implicitly
- **Mirror** — no repo data gets placed on a cluster implicitly

Those two stay as `✗` rows in the closing checklist with their `run later:` hints. That's the "non-interactive contract": `--yes` (and no-TTY runs) may do local setup on your behalf, but account and server-side actions require you to either run them interactively or invoke them explicitly.

Which is also why the cluster question never conflicts with `--yes`: the mirror offer simply doesn't run in that mode, and the new cluster resolution only prompts on an interactive terminal — scripts always get the stable fixed default.

- **One-shot** (`entire repo mirror create <github-url>` with no cluster): a **single-select** picker, jurisdiction-preselected. Built for "mirror this one repo".

The enable offer mirrors exactly one repo — the origin — so I reused the one-shot's resolution, and there it genuinely *is* the same code: `chooseClusterHost` → `pickOneCluster` is now literally shared between the one-shot command and the offer, not a copy. - `is_default` is deliberately per-jurisdiction, so pre-checking can't fan a repo into every region by accident.

**Trail 3 is ready for your review** — and it turned out even cleaner than expected: `status --json` never exposed a strategy field, so this is purely a human-output change. Uncommitted (except the cherry-picked tokenstore test fix), on branch `feat/status-drop-strategy-name` off `main`:

**Before → after:**

```
● Enabled · manual-commit · branch main        ● Enabled · branch main
  Agents · Claude Code                           Agents · Claude Code

Project · enabled · manual-commit              Project · enabled
Local · disabled · manual-commit               Local · disabled
```

The diff is tiny: both status formatters drop the strategy segment (with a comment saying why — it's the only strategy, so naming it answers no user question), the now-unused `strategy` import removed, and six tests flipped from "must show manual-commit" to "must *not* show manual-commit" (including `TestRunStatus_ShowsManualCommitStrategy` renamed to `TestRunStatus_HidesStrategyName`). Full suite green — 8,103 tests.

Note this branch also carries a cherry-pick of the tokenstore test fix (the Go 1.26 `-json` stderr thing) since main doesn't have it yet and the suite can't pass without it — it'll land on main faster through this small PR than through the big onboarding one.

Approve and I'll commit, push, and create the trail (PR targeting `main` directly, since this doesn't depend on onboarding). Or if you want to eyeball it live first: I can build `entire-demo` from this branch briefly — though it lacks the onboarding trails, so simplest is just trusting the before/after above.
